added_failures_note: The reviewed manifest records no baseline_suite and no after_suite arm (both null in the run's own classification.json). Its single gate.log names head revision 6d3d51576 and shows 2467 passed, 0 failed, EXIT=0, which this review reproduced exactly at the same head (2467 passed, 11 skipped, 5 deselected, EXIT=0). A head arm with no failing id cannot have added a failure, so added_failure_count reads 0 with no ids. No base arm was measured, so no base/head subtraction was possible.

findings.text: follow-on: the ingest claim reads the same four scope fields the triage (names) arm writes, with no relevance_stage filter, so a file whose content-arm decision failed is still admitted whenever its name-arm relevance already reaches the ingest threshold. CODE_RELEVANCE_EXPR (scorer.py:63) is the max over relevance_loads/processes/describes/imas regardless of stage, and _claim_code_files_for_ingestion at workers.py:650-657 filters only on status='scored' AND that expression >= $min_relevance AND line_count. The plan says 'ingest admits a file when its content relevance is at least code-ingest-threshold'; the triage arm writes relevance at code-triage-threshold 0.4 (default) and the ingest threshold is 0.5, so any file the names arm rated >= 0.5 keeps that value after a failed or skipped content decision. TRIGGERING INPUT: a file with a successful names-arm decision at relevance 0.7, then a content decision that fails (the score_worker content call is wrapped in return_exceptions=True and simply drops it) -- relevance_stage stays 'name', relevance_loads stays 0.7, and the next ingest pass claims the file on the name relevance, so it is never retried by the content arm. The node's own test test_ingest_claims_highest_relevance_first_and_refuses_below_threshold seeds rows with relevance_loads and no relevance_stage and asserts they ARE claimed, i.e. the shipped suite demonstrates the claim is stage-agnostic. Contrasts with the triage arm's fail-closed path, which correctly leaves the file and releases the claim.

follow-on: claim_files_for_scoring's read-back still selects sf.triage_description AS triage_description, a CodeFile property the same node retired from imas_codex/schemas/facility.yaml. Cypher returns null for an absent property rather than erroring, so the run is unaffected, but this is the one reader of the retired field the plan's 'every reader migrates in the same node: ... graph_ops.py ...' did not remove. Nothing consumes the returned key either: _build_score_user_prompt no longer reads it (the triage_desc block was deleted) and _group_files_by_parent no longer copies it into file_entry. TRIGGERING INPUT: none functionally -- it is dead. The cost is that graph_ops.py, scorer.py and facility.yaml now disagree about whether CodeFile carries triage_description, and a future reader grepping for the retired field finds a live-looking read.

follow-on: the score_worker comment 'A failure here leaves the file scored with no content relevance, so the ingest claim refuses it and a later pass can retry' is false as written. 'no content relevance' is inaccurate -- the triage arm already wrote relevance_loads/processes/describes/imas with relevance_stage='name', and those fields survive a failed content decision -- and 'the ingest claim refuses it' holds only when the name-arm relevance is below code-ingest-threshold. TRIGGERING INPUT: same as the first finding -- a name-arm relevance >= 0.5 plus a failed content decision is admitted, not refused. A comment that states a guarantee the code does not provide is the shape this review is meant to catch; the mechanism as implemented is 'a failed content decision leaves the name-arm relevance in place', which is a weaker claim.

follow-on: _group_files_by_parent builds the sibling-group key as `pid = row["path"] and row["parent_id"]` where it was `row["parent_id"]`. Both keys come from the same RETURN (`pid AS parent_id, cf.path AS path`), and cf.path is a required property, so the left operand is always truthy and the expression evaluates to row["parent_id"] exactly as before. It is a no-op guarded by a value that cannot be falsy here; if the intent was a null guard on parent_id, the operands are swapped. No behavioural impact (all sibling-name and claim tests pass), flagged only because the form invites a reader to look for a case it handles.

justifications.durability: The mechanism is the durable shape: one decisions route reused from the call node, one CODE_RELEVANCE_EXPR shared by the triage gate, the enrich gate, the ingest gate, the pending-work predicates and the stats query, the questions declared once in the template and loaded through render_prompt, and a validation-failure path that leaves the file unclaimed for retry. Two deductions. The content gate is not actually fail-closed: the ingest claim reads relevance with no stage filter, so a failed content decision falls back to the name-arm relevance rather than refusing the file, which weakens the guarantee the plan asks for. And the retired mechanism leaves live-looking residue -- the triage_description read-back in graph_ops.py:530 and the retained FileTriageResult/FileTriageBatch/apply-adjacent surface -- that a later reader must re-derive as dead.
justifications.evidence: The gate the manifest names is recorded in gate.log and I reproduced it at head (2467 passed, EXIT=0) and its negative control independently (EXIT=1, exactly the two triage assertions red, content arm green); the decisions-questions template renders six keys through render_prompt, verified by probe. The new test file drives both arms through the fake HTTP seam and asserts the query the worker actually issued, so the guarded triage comparison is exercised in both directions. Two deductions: the reviewed record carries no baseline/after arm, so its measured added-failure pair is absent and added_failure_count is derived as 0 from the zero-failure head arm alone; and the ingest test seeds stage-less rows and confirms the claim admits them, which is the fail-open rather than a check on it.
justifications.fit: The added symbols are mechanism-named (triage_relevance, SCOPE_NOULS, relevance_stage, CODE_RELEVANCE_EXPR, get_code_ingest_threshold), the template wording and the graph schema descriptions are carried over and rewritten in the file's own register, and the commits are conventional with bodies carrying no plan identifier and no attribution. Two deductions: the score_worker comment claims the ingest claim refuses a content-failed file, which the code does not do, and the sibling-group key uses an 'and' whose operands read as swapped.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The node does what the plan asked: triage.md rewritten in place as the decisions template with the six questions; CodeFile's eleven triage fields removed and the eight relevance fields added, followed by build-models; the discovery-triage seat replaced by discovery-relevance in cli/discover/code.py; get_triage_threshold replaced by get_code_triage_threshold in code and the retired naming gone from state.py and parallel.py; TRIAGE_DIMENSION_NAMES removed; _CODE_TRIAGE_FIELDS replaced by _CODE_RELEVANCE_FIELDS; the two settings added under [tool.imas-codex.discovery]; is_simulation recorded but not a gate and role not a gate; and the named tests updated. Two deductions, both the ingest-gate deviation: the plan says ingest admits on the file's content relevance, but a failed content decision leaves the name-arm relevance in place and the claim admits on that, so 'the deployed content-arm ingest gate' is not enforced on the failure path; and the graph_ops triage_description reader was not migrated.
justifications.reuse: Strong. call_decisions/acall_decisions from the decisions-call node are reused rather than a second route; _service_headers, _is_retryable and the facility data_access_patterns source are shared with the existing paths; CODE_RELEVANCE_EXPR is written once and interpolated into six queries so every gate measures the same quantity; _RELEVANCE_FIELDS maps the decision question names to the CodeFile fields in one place; and _relevance_item is shared by the triage and content persistence helpers. One deduction for the residual read of the retired triage_description in graph_ops.py, which is reuse of a field the same node deleted.
